papers.title: The Energy-Dependence of GRB Minimum Variability Timescales (title verified from the PDF title page and ADS; NOT 'On the Rapid Variability of GRBs', which is Golkhou & Butler 2014 Paper I)

papers.verbatim_anchor: Table 2 ('GRB Minimum Timescales'), PDF p. 24, word-coordinate verified: '110618366 | 110618A | 12.874 +/- 0.363 | 1.755 +/- 0.152 | 163.843 +/- 11.406 | -59.600 | 241.866 | 0.54 | 0.07 | ...' = dt_min, dt_S/N, T90, T_start_100, T_stop_100, sigma_X(tmin), sigma_X(tS/N), z(none)
papers.definition_note_T3: dt_min = the timescale at which the Haar-wavelet scaleogram sigma_X(dt) departs from the linear (uncorrelated-noise) rise, fitted with a broken power law - NOT a pulse width and NOT our MVT estimator; dt_S/N is the Poisson-noise floor, the shortest MEASURABLE timescale. Band: light curves extracted at 200 microsecond binning over the FULL 8 keV - 1 MeV GBM range (they also work in 4 log-spaced channels 8-26 / 26-89 / 89-299 / 299-1000 keV, but Table 2 is the full-band value). Copy the definition AND the band with the number or the diff is meaningless.
papers.not_independent_note: their T90 column is INHERITED from von Kienlin+2014 Table 7 (stated in their Sect. 2: T90 estimates used for background windows come from 'Table 7 of von Kienlin et al. (2014)') - which is why 163.843 +/- 11.406 matches to 3 decimals. Do NOT count it as an independent duration measurement.
papers.internal_flag_T5: dt_S/N = 1.755 +/- 0.152 is numerically IDENTICAL to the neighbouring row (110613631). Recorded as-is and flagged as a possible quantization/duplication artifact - re-verify at source before using it in any correlation.
